conclusion: The partial handler cannot interoperate with the normal logical ALLOC alignment 8 because it honestly exposes only 4096/65536 page-backed alignment, and its first MAP fixes page size for the owner session. H2D remains the existing v1 memory carrier, while SUBMIT and type-20 completion must remain unsupported until queue, signal, packet, CRC, and nonzero lifecycle ticks are owner-bound end to end.
decision: Resolve logical-versus-backing alignment without falsifying the ACK, bind v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D to the same generic owner/allocation session, preserve the owner-session-fixed page-size restriction until deliberately changed, and implement queue/signal/AQL packet/tick plus cancellation and disconnect semantics before enabling SUBMIT or advertising bit 8.
invalidated_assumptions: Accepting ALLOC alignment 8 is safe when the native response reports its 4096-byte backing alignment.
Generic dispatch needs or may invent a separate KERNARG wire opcode instead of retaining v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D.
A local native CP admission result is sufficient to emit a successful SUBMIT ACK or type-20 completion without queue, signal, packet CRC, and nonzero tick identities.
observation: The CP24 route harness accepts 4K/64K page policy, rejects ALLOC alignment 8 and every SUBMIT, and records page_size_lifetime=owner-session-fixed. Existing runtime mock evidence carries kernarg bytes through sealed-FD v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D, but no live gem5 daemon H2D route, successful SUBMIT ACK, or type-20 completion is retained.
question_or_symptom: Why can CP24 expose MAP/ALLOC/H2D/UNMAP handler source while still refusing the ordinary runtime allocation and every SUBMIT?
